title: (Invited) Generalized GPU-Accelerated Dynamic Programming with Application to Mixed-Cell-Height Detailed Placement
problem: Dynamic programming algorithms with quadratic or higher time complexities face scalability challenges in large-scale physical design applications like placement.
motivation: DP methods are fundamental to many optimization algorithms in physical design but their computational complexity limits practical applicability.
method: The approach speeds up dynamic programming problems by using graphics processors (GPUs), which can perform many calculations simultaneously instead of one at a time. It works by breaking the expensive cost calculations into independent pieces that run in parallel across the GPU's cores, then efficiently combines these results back together. This is demonstrated on the practical problem of optimally arranging electronic components of different sizes on a computer chip.
key_novelty: The main contribution is a general GPU acceleration framework for any dynamic programming algorithm in chip design.
contributions: Average 96.6% runtime reduction on placement tasks
General technique applicable to other physical design algorithms
limitations: Presented as case study on detailed placement; generalization to other DP applications requires further work.
primary_theme: GPU-accelerated DP for physical design optimization
